info.title: PerfScope API
info.description:
Every route the backend serves, what it is for, and whether it needs a token. Kept honest by
`apps/backend/src/routes/routes.contract.test.ts`, which fails when a route is added, moved
or removed without this file changing.

**Machine-readable:** [`openapi.json`](openapi.json) (OpenAPI 3.1) is generated from these
tables and the `@perfscope/shared` types — run `pnpm openapi` in `apps/backend` after changing
either, and `apps/backend/openapi/operations.ts` says which type each route answers with. CI
fails on a stale spec, and `e2e/openapi-conformance.probe.mjs` validates real responses
against it.

Generated from `docs/api/README.md` and the `@perfscope/shared` types by `apps/backend/openapi/build.mts` — edit those, never this file.

Prometheus text format. Internal by default; `METRICS_TOKEN` guards it where the port is exposed. See [OBSERVABILITY.md](../deploy/OBSERVABILITY.md).

bearerAuth.description: Access token from /api/auth/login, /register or /refresh. Lasts 30 minutes.

TeamId.name: X-Team-Id
TeamId.description: Act inside a team: the request is resolved to the team owner's account.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or expired access token.

headline.description: At most a dozen words — the one useful thing to say right now.

steps.description: Ordered by what to do first. Empty when there is nothing to act on.

AiAdvice.description:
What the advisor says about whatever the user is currently looking at.

Structured rather than prose because it drives a panel that is on screen continuously: a headline you can read at a glance and up to three steps in the order they should be done. Prose at that frequency turns into wallpaper.

url.description: One of the user's own site URLs.

AiAdviceAction.description: A closed set on purpose. The model picks a `kind`, and the server checks the `url` against sites the user actually has before it goes out — a link invented from nothing is worse than no link.

action.description:
Where this step can actually be carried out, when it maps to something the app does.

Advice that says "audit example.com" and leaves you to find the analyzer is a note; the same advice with somewhere to click is a step. Absent when the step is something the user does outside PerfScope — most fixes are.

AiMetricNotes.description: A short note per Core Web Vital, keyed by the vital. Only non-good vitals get one.

formFactor.description: Device profile the audit ran with; absent on results saved before the toggle existed.

aiInsights.description: Three prioritised fixes for the page as a whole.

aiMetricNotes.description: Per-vital commentary, for the vitals that are not already good.

aiWaterfallNarrative.description: Two or three sentences narrating how this page actually loaded.

authRedirectDetected.description: Set when Lighthouse was redirected to an auth/login page instead of the requested URL.

measurement.description: Present when the run was measured more than once (median reporting).

thirdParty.description: Vendors loaded by the page, heaviest first.

previous.description: The previous run of this URL, and what changed since it. Absent when there is none.

bundles.description: What the page's JavaScript is made of. Absent when the page ships none.

screenshot.description:
A cropped picture of the failing element, as a `data:image/jpeg` URI.

Cropped out of Lighthouse's full-page capture during the audit, so it costs no request at read time and a stored audit keeps it. Present only where a run captured elements (the socket path, where a person is watching) and only for details that named a node.

AuditDetail.description: One flagged item from a Lighthouse audit's `details.items`, normalised across the shapes Lighthouse uses: `node.selector`/`node.snippet` for DOM audits, `url` for network ones, a wasted-bytes/wasted-ms/total-bytes figure for opportunities.

AuditFormFactor.description: Which device profile a Lighthouse run emulated.

description.description: Lighthouse's own documentation for this audit — generic, identical on every site.

category.description:
Which Lighthouse category reported this audit — the four the analyzer scores.

Optional because audits stored before this field existed have none, and the filter UI hides itself rather than showing a control that would silently drop every older row.

group.description: Lighthouse's own grouping *inside* that category, as its display title — "Contrast", "Names and labels", "Diagnostics". Accessibility is the category where it earns its keep: forty findings sorted by severity alone are a list, the same forty under their groups are a to-do list. Not every audit belongs to a group.

aiExplanation.description:
What this failure means *on this page*, and the first thing to do about it.

Absent when Gemini is not configured, when the call failed, or when the audit passed (only failing audits are explained — explaining a pass costs a token and says nothing).

details.description: The first few things this audit flagged on this page — the selector, the request, the value. Capped: an audit with 300 unlabelled images explains itself in three.

savingsMs.description: Lighthouse's own estimate of this audit's total impact — `overallSavingsMs` / `overallSavingsBytes` off the raw LHR, present only on "opportunity" audits that compute one (most diagnostics don't). Previously only reachable as unstructured text inside `displayValue`; kept numeric so a fix can be ranked by real impact instead of a model's own guess at severity.

AuditSource.description: Who asked for a run: a person, or the site's timetable.

AuthAuditSessionResponse.description: `POST /api/auth-audit/session` — the handle for the visible browser it just opened.

token.description: Short-lived (30 minutes). Sent as the Bearer on every request.

refreshToken.description:
Long-lived (30 days), opaque, and rotated every time it is spent.

The pair exists so the access token can afford to be short: a leaked token is useful for half an hour instead of a month, and a session can be ended server-side, which a stateless JWT cannot be. Clients store it beside the access token and trade it in at `POST /auth/refresh` when a request comes back 401.

AuthResponse.description:
What every way in answers with: password login, registration and Google sign-in all return the same pair, so a caller never has to know which door it came through.

Five places described this inline — both auth pages twice each and GoogleButton — which is how a field could be renamed on one route and noticed on none.

AutomationScheduleMode.description:
How a site's routes are distributed across the day.
- `single` — every route in one block at `scheduleTime` (the original behaviour)
- `slots`  — explicit groups: /checkout at 02:00, /blog at 14:00
- `spread` — all routes fanned out evenly across `spreadMinutes` from `scheduleTime`

AutomationSlot.description: A group of routes and the time of day they are audited.

formFactor.description: `null` on stored breaches (the schema defaults it), absent on documents from before the field existed. This used to be typed `AuditFormFactor` here and `string | null` on the backend — the client type didn't describe what the backend actually writes.

BudgetBreach.description: Set when the latest audit broke the site's budgets; cleared once the same URL passes.

BudgetFailure.description:
One lab budget that a stored audit broke.

Only these four: `Website.budgets` also accepts `inp`, but no lab run can measure it, so it is checked against RUM p75 in rumBudget.service — which raises an alert and never writes `lastBudgetBreach`. The union used to claim inp/fcp/ttfb as well, which nothing could ever produce here.

unusedBytes.description: Bytes never executed during the load, where coverage could tell.

BundleNode.description:
One node of a script's module tree — a directory, a package, or a single source file.

Sizes are *resource* bytes (uncompressed, as the engine parses them), because that is what "unused" is measured against and what a bundler's own output reports. The transfer size lives on the script, where compression actually applies.

duplicates.description: Modules that appear in more than one bundle, heaviest first.

BundleSummary.description:
What the page's JavaScript is made of.

Lighthouse computes this on every performance run (`script-treemap-data`, an informative audit of weight 0) from source maps and coverage, and PerfScope dropped it. "Reduce unused JavaScript — 612 KB" is a number; "lodash, 71 KB, 64% unused, inside vendor.js" is a fix.

aiVerdict.description: Two or three sentences on who wins and what to attack first, written when the comparison was saved. Absent for comparisons stored before this existed, and whenever Gemini was unavailable.

CompareEntry.description: One stored side-by-side comparison run, as served by /api/compare-history.

ComparisonSide.description: One side of a stored comparison. Loose maps rather than the strict score/vital shapes on purpose: a side can arrive from an uploaded report as well as a live run, and the stored rows predate today's field lists. This shape used to be written out inline in seven places across the backend and this file.

CompetitorSessionEntry.description:
A rival's captured session, from `GET /api/competitor-sessions`.

Same redaction as a Website's: `session` says only that cookies were captured and when.

scope.description: The exact page when CrUX has URL-level data, otherwise the whole origin.

collectedFrom.description: Collection window reported by the API (YYYY-MM-DD).

p75.description: 75th percentile — the value Google grades the metric on.

good.description: Share of samples in each bucket, 0–1.

at.description: When it went out. Supplied by the caller — CI records a deploy after the fact.

ref.description: Commit sha, tag, build number — whatever the pipeline knows itself by.

label.description: Human label: "v2.4.0", "hotfix: cart". Falls back to a short `ref` on the chart.

url.description: Where to read about it — a commit, a PR, a pipeline run.

Deploy.description:
A deployment, recorded so a chart can say *why* a line moved.

A performance chart shows that something changed on the eleventh; it cannot show that the eleventh is when the image loader was swapped. Without that, reading a regression means going to the git log with a date in hand and guessing. Marking releases on the chart turns "something got worse" into "this got worse after that", which is the whole question anyone has when they open the page.

DeployInput.description: What a caller may send. Everything but the site is optional: a bare "we deployed" is still worth more on a chart than nothing.

DiffableResource.description:
The shape of "what changed between two runs of the same page".

The *algorithm* stays in `apps/backend/src/lib/resourceDiff.ts` — it needs URL parsing and noise thresholds that only the server applies. What lives here is the wire shape, because the diff is no longer only prompt evidence: it is attached to the result as `AnalysisResult.previous.resourceDiff` and rendered by the analyzer, so the browser needs the type without pulling the server's implementation across the boundary.

DigestPreference.description: Weekly-summary preference. `day` is 0–6 with 0 = Sunday, `time` is 'HH:MM' local to the viewer. A user created before the feature existed has none stored and reads as defaults.

path.description: Path with its query string, as the sitemap gives it.

priority.description: 0–1, when the sitemap says — the site telling us what it thinks matters.

DiscoveredRoute.description: One page a site's sitemap claims to have.

FieldMetricKey.description:
The metrics real users produce, as opposed to the ones a lab run measures.

CrUX and our own RUM collector report exactly these five, and both had declared the union separately — as did the dashboard, a third time. Derived from VitalKey so a metric cannot be a field metric without being a vital with thresholds.

Note what is absent: tbt, si and tti are lab-only (no browser reports them from a real visit), and inp is the mirror image — field-only, which is why a lab budget on it can never fire.

FlowActionKind.description: What a step does to the page before it is measured.

FlowAuditItem.description: Deliberately not `AuditItem`: a flow report shows far less per audit, and importing the analyzer's full item would drag element screenshots and savings into a document that never displays them.

websiteId.description: The site this belongs to, when it was created from one.

url.description: Where the flow starts. Every flow opens with a cold navigation here.

snapshotAtEnd.description: Audit the page as it is at the end, for the accessibility of whatever state the flow left behind. Cheap — a snapshot takes no timing — and usually the point of the flow.

lastRun.description: Set by the API when listing: when this flow last ran, and how it went.

url.description: Where the flow starts. Every flow opens with a cold navigation here.

snapshotAtEnd.description: Audit the page as it is at the end, for the accessibility of whatever state the flow left behind. Cheap — a snapshot takes no timing — and usually the point of the flow.

websiteId.description: The site this belongs to, when it was created from one.

FlowInput.description: What a client sends to create or replace a flow (`POST /api/flows`, `PUT /api/flows/:id`) — the definition without anything the server owns.

durationMs.description: Wall clock for the whole flow, which is what a person waits for.

time.description: Server-local `HH:MM`, matched by the cron the same way nightly audits are.

FlowSchedule.description:
When a flow runs on its own.

One time a day rather than the website automation's slots/spread machinery: a flow is a scripted journey through a page, and running the same journey six times a day tells you about the site's noise, not about the journey. The nightly audit already answers "how is it now"; this answers "did what we changed today make the checkout slower".

selector.description: CSS selector. Required for click/type/hover/waitFor, meaningless for the rest.

value.description: Text to type, key to press, pixels to scroll, milliseconds to wait, URL to navigate.

name.description: What this step is called in the report. Defaults to a description of the action.

measure.description:
Whether this step is measured on its own.

Default true, and that default is the point: a flow whose steps are all measured together reports one number for five interactions and cannot say which one was slow. Turn it off for the plumbing — a cookie banner to dismiss, a field to fill before the button that matters — so the report stays about the interactions worth reading.

FlowStepMode.description: The measurement modes, named as Lighthouse names them.

scores.description: Only the categories this mode actually scores.

audits.description: Failing audits, capped per category exactly as a navigation audit's are.

action.description: What the step did, echoed back so a report reads without the definition beside it.

FlowStepResult.description:
What one measured step produced.

Everything past `mode` is optional because the modes genuinely differ — a timespan has no LCP and a snapshot has no timing at all. A reader that assumes otherwise renders a confident zero, which is the one thing a measuring tool must not do.

FlowTargets.description:
What a flow promises about itself.

Ceilings over the *measured interactions*, not over the page load — the navigation step is an ordinary audit and the site's own budgets already cover it. INP is the reason this exists: it is field-only everywhere else in the product (see `targets.ts`), so a flow is the only place a lab number can be held to a threshold.

source.description: Absent on audits stored before the distinction existed — those were all manual.

scores.description: Performance score of every iteration, in run order.

median.description: Score of the run whose artifacts this result carries.

spread.description: max − min across iterations; large values mean the page measures unreliably.

MeasurementQuality.description: How the reported performance numbers were produced. A single Lighthouse run swings by ±10 points on the same page, so anything derived from one shot (trends, regressions, budget breaches) is partly noise. When `runs > 1` the reported result is the median run and `spread` says how noisy the page is.

lines.description: Human-readable bullets, exactly as they were sent.

unread.description: Raised since this account last opened the bell.

NotificationEntry.description:
One entry in the bell.

The same alerts the dashboard's incident list is built from, but ordered by time rather than by whether they are still open — the bell answers "what happened", not "what is broken", and a recovery is as much news as a breach.

unread.description: How many of them are unread — the badge. Counted server-side over the whole log, not over the returned page, so a busy account does not under-report.

seenAt.description: When the account last opened the bell; null if never.

steps.description: Per-step completion, keyed by step id.

counts.description: Convenience counts the panel shows as evidence ("2 sites, 14 audits").

complete.description: True once every step is done — the panel retires itself.

score.description: The site's mean performance score, or null when it has never been audited.

detail.description: One line of specifics, e.g. "LCP 4.9s over 2.5s budget".

OverviewAttentionReason.description: Why a site is listed as needing action. Ordered by how actionable it is.

delta.description: Points against the previous successful run of the same URL; null when it is the first.

routePath.description: The path alone, for a compact row: the host is already obvious from the site list.

days.description: Window length in days, so the UI can label itself without hardcoding it.

from.description: The window the server actually counted, as calendar days. Sent back because the picker can ask for a range that gets clamped — a chart labelled with what was requested rather than what was measured is a chart that lies about its own axis.

rum.description: null when no site has a RUM key — the card then explains what installing it gives.

url.description: The audited page, not the site root — budgets are checked per URL.

aiNote.description: What Gemini said when this alert was sent. Absent on alerts raised without AI.

OverviewIncident.description:
An alert that fired and has not recovered.

`delivery` is the point: an incident with an empty array was recorded but never left the server, because no channel was configured or every channel failed. Without showing that, "I never got an alert" is unanswerable.

sitesReporting.description: Sites that reported at least one page view in the window.

sitesInstalled.description: Sites with a snippet key issued, whether or not anything has arrived.

sites.description: Sites tracked, regardless of whether they have ever been audited.

audited.description: Sites with at least one successful audit — the denominator for `avgScore`.

avgScore.description: Mean performance score across audited sites. 0 when nothing has been audited.

needsAttention.description: Audited sites scoring below the poor threshold.

auditsInWindow.description:
Successful audits recorded inside the selected window.

Named for what it is rather than for its old fixed seven days: the window is a control on the page now, and a field called `audits7d` holding ninety days of them is the kind of name that survives long enough to mislead someone.

OverviewTotals.description:
The account-wide dashboard payload.

One request rather than one per site: the page needs alerts, audits and field traffic across every site the user owns, and doing that client-side would be 1 + 2N requests that all have to land before anything can be ranked.

OverviewTrendPoint.description: One day of one site's history. `score` is null on days with no successful run.

OverviewVitalSplit.description:
How every audited page falls into the web.dev bands for one metric.

Counts runs, not sites: the question it answers is "which metric is most often the problem", and a site audited fifty times should weigh more than one audited once.

Paginated_WebsiteDoc.description:
A page of results and where it sits in the whole.

Generic in the item because the two ends hold different things: the server has mongoose documents with ObjectIds and Dates, the client has what JSON made of them. The envelope is the part both must agree on, and the part that had drifted — so the server annotates `Paginated<IWebsite>` and the client `WebsitePage`, and a renamed field breaks both.

`page` is the page actually served, which is not always the one asked for: the route counts first and clamps, so requesting page 99 of 3 answers page 3 rather than an empty list that claims to be page 99.

analysisId.description: Identifies the compared-against run, so the UI can link straight to it.

resourceDiff.description: Resource-level movement. Absent when nothing crossed the noise floors.

newAuditIds.description: Ids of audits failing now that were not failing then.

fixedAudits.description: Audits that were failing then and are not in this run's list any more.

PreviousRunSummary.description:
The run this one is compared against — what moved, and what shipped that moved it.

Attached server-side before `analysis:complete` is emitted and stored with the result, so the live view, a reopened history row, the public report and the CLI all describe the same comparison. The client never fetches the previous run itself: two clients asking at different times would compare against different runs and disagree about the same audit.

Absent when there is no earlier audit of this URL for this owner *at the same form factor* — a desktop run is not the predecessor of a mobile one.

source.description: Absent on audits stored before the distinction existed — those were all manual.

sharedAt.description: When the audit was stored (the History row's `createdAt`) — not when the link was minted.

PublicReport.description: `GET /api/public/report/:token` — the stored result behind a share link.

ResourceResize.description: One resource that changed size between the two runs.

sources.description: Which sitemaps answered. "We found nothing" and "there is no sitemap" are different answers, and the reader can only act on one of them.

reason.description: Set when nothing could be read at all.

key.description: Public site key identifying which Website this belongs to.

path.description: Path only — query strings and fragments are dropped before they leave the page.

device.description: Coarse device class, derived from viewport width.

v.description: Collector version, so a payload shape change is diagnosable server-side.

RumBeacon.description: What the collector beacons. Kept small: it travels on the visitor's connection.

RumMetricKey.description: Our collector reports the same five metrics CrUX does — deliberately, see above.

p75.description: 75th percentile — the value Google grades the metric on.

good.description: Share of samples in each bucket, 0–1.

samples.description: How many page views contributed this metric.

RumMetricSummary.description:
Field data for one metric, from our own collector.

Structurally CrUX's shape plus a sample count — deliberately, so the Field data tab can render either source through the same components. Extending says so rather than leaving two identical blocks to drift.

lcp.description: p75 LCP for that path, or null when no sample carried one.

RumPathRow.description: Busiest paths in the window, so the dashboard can show where the traffic is.

rumKey.description: null until the user has generated a snippet for this site.

RumResponse.description: `GET /api/websites/:id/rum` — everything the Field data tab needs in one request.

scope.description: Whole site, or a single path when one was requested.

device.description: Both device classes together, or one when filtered.

pageViews.description: Distinct page views in the window — the denominator for every metric.

RumTrendPoint.description: One day of field data for a single metric.

ScheduledSiteReport.description:
One site's scheduled runs, in the shape the project page already renders.

Deliberately the same type rather than a parallel one: the scheduled page is that page repeated per site, so it reuses RouteGroupCard, the audit table and the stat strip instead of inventing a second way to show the same thing.

transferBytes.description: Over the wire, when Lighthouse knew it — compression usually makes this much smaller.

hasSourceMap.description: Whether a source map let Lighthouse see inside; without one there are no modules.

modules.description: The pruned module tree. Absent when the script has no source map.

role.description: The caller's own role, not the team's. A list is read to decide where to work.

TeamInviteInfo.description:
An outstanding invitation.

`url` is present exactly once — in the response that mints it. The token is stored hashed, the same way refresh tokens and password resets are, so a listing can name an invite and revoke it but can never hand out the link again.

valid.description: False when it is spent or past its date — the page says so instead of failing on accept.

TeamInvitePreview.description: What the accept page shows before anyone commits to anything.

TeamMemberInfo.description: A person on a team, as the members list shows them.

role.description: The caller's own role, not the team's. A list is read to decide where to work.

TeamSummary.description: A team in a list — enough to switch to it and to say what you can do there.

name.description: Vendor name as Lighthouse identifies it (e.g. "Google Tag Manager").

mainThreadTime.description: Total main-thread time attributed to this vendor (ms).

blockingTime.description: Portion of main-thread time that blocked interactivity (ms).

ThirdPartyEntity.description: Per-vendor cost, from Lighthouse's third-party-summary audit.

networkOffsetMs.description: ms from navigationStart to the earliest network request

VitalKey.description:
Metric thresholds per web.dev ("good" is inclusive).

Covers both what a lab run measures (tbt, si, tti) and what only real users can produce (inp, ttfb) — field data buckets its samples against the same numbers, so they live together rather than in a second table.

routes.description: Every route the site audits. Stays the canonical list in all three modes.

scheduleTime.description: Start of the run in `single`, start of the window in `spread`.

scheduleMode.description: Absent on documents written before slots existed — read it as 'single'.

spreadMinutes.description: Window length in minutes for `spread`; 60 means "all of them within an hour".

WebsiteAutomation.description: Generic in the date because these types are the single definition for both ends of the wire: the backend's Mongoose documents hold real `Date`s, the client holds what JSON made of them. The backend aliases (`IWebsiteAutomation` etc. in Website.model.ts) bind `D = Date`; everything else defaults to the string the client sees. Before this the backend kept hand-written mirrors, and they had already drifted.

inp.description: Maximum acceptable INP in ms. Field-only — no lab run produces this metric.

webhookUrl.description: POSTed a BudgetBreach payload whenever an audit violates the budgets.

alertEmail.description: Receives a breach summary email (requires SMTP_* configured on the backend).

WebsiteBudgets.description: Per-site performance budgets; a metric is checked only when its threshold is set.

rumKey.description: Public key embedded in the RUM snippet — visible in page source by design. Served by the website routes but absent until the user asks for a snippet.

WebsiteLoginWall.description: Set when an audit was redirected to a login screen; cleared once that same URL audits cleanly.

WebsiteSession.description:
A captured session, as the client is allowed to see it: that one exists, and when it was taken. The cookies and localStorage behind it are live credentials for the audited site and never leave the backend — they live in `models/session.schema.ts`, and the `toJSON` transform there strips them from every response.

Whether a session still *works* is a separate question, answered by `requiresLogin`; see `sessionState()` on the dashboard, which needs both.

WebsiteSummary.description:
The headline strip above the website list, from `GET /api/websites/summary`.

Deliberately ignores the list's search term so the numbers stay put while the user types. `avgScore` is 0 for an account with no successful audits, not null — the tile always shows a number.
